Architecture Review Board: Payments Platform

Owner: Payments Engineering. Business purpose: process customer card and wallet payments in production. Criticality: critical. Data classification: restricted. Environments: production and staging in Example Cloud region-1 and region-2.

Actors

  • Customer — human user initiating payments from the web application
  • Payments administrator — internal operator with privileged console access
  • External payment processor — third-party acquirer receiving settlement batches

Components and data stores

NameTypeDescription
Web ApplicationWeb UICustomer-facing checkout experience
Payments APIAPIPublic REST API validating and orchestrating payments
Identity ProviderIdentityOAuth 2.0 authorization server with MFA
Payment QueueQueueAsynchronous settlement and retry processing
Payment Records DBDatabasePostgreSQL storing payment tokens and amounts encrypted at rest
Session CacheCacheRedis cache for short-lived checkout sessions

Data flows

  1. Customer browser to Web Application over HTTPS with OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens
  2. Web Application to Payments API over HTTPS with mutual TLS inside the VPC
  3. Payments API to Identity Provider over HTTPS for token validation
  4. Payments API to Payment Records DB over TLS/PostgreSQL using workload identity
  5. Payments API to Payment Queue over TLS/AMQP for settlement jobs
  6. Payment Queue to External payment processor over HTTPS with signed webhooks

Trust boundaries and entry points

Production network boundary contains the Web Application, Payments API, queue, databases, and cache. DMZ boundary exposes only the public Payments API HTTPS endpoint and the customer web entry point. External entry point: public Payments API on HTTPS with OAuth 2.0 and MFA for administrators. Internal entry point: admin console restricted to corporate SSO.

Authentication and authorization

Customers authenticate through the identity provider using OAuth 2.0 authorization code with PKCE. Administrators require MFA. Service-to-service calls use workload identity and scoped service accounts. Database access is role-based and limited to the Payments API service account.

Deployment

Deployment type: cloud (Example Cloud). Provider-managed Kubernetes runs the Web Application, Payments API, and queue workers. Managed PostgreSQL and Redis provide persistence. Regions: region-1 (primary) and region-2 (DR). Backups: encrypted daily snapshots retained 35 days.

Assumptions

  • The architecture document represents the current production baseline.
  • All external integrations use TLS 1.2 or higher.
  • Token lifetimes follow the identity provider defaults unless noted otherwise.
